body:
Port the multi-lens adversarial P5 prosecution architecture from plugins/adlc-claude-code to plugins/adlc-codex. Today Codex's P5 review is a single generic agent (plugins/adlc-codex/agents/adlc-reviewer.toml) that mixes correctness, security, contract-drift, and hollow-test concerns into one prompt with no fan-out, no cross-lens dedupe, and no independent verification. Claude Code's equivalent (plugins/adlc-claude-code/agents/prosecutor{,-correctness,-security,-contract,-diff,-tests,-verifier}.md) fans out five independent read-only lens subagents, dedupes findings, verifies each deduped finding independently (majority vote via survivesVerification), and loops until two consecutive dry rounds (shouldContinue) — all backed by pure orchestration helpers in @adlc/core (re-exported via plugins/adlc-claude-code/lib/prosecutor.mjs). Bring the same behavior natively to Codex.

=== CONTRACT (write then gate) ===
Author .adlc/specs/codex-prosecutor-fanout.md as the binding P1 spec before coding. It must pin: the five lens definitions and their exact hunting briefs (correctness, security, contract, diff, tests — same failure classes as the Claude Code lenses, reworded only where Codex TOML agent conventions require it), the JSON finding schema each lens returns, how the orchestrating skill invokes each lens agent plus the verifier natively in Codex (Codex has no primitive identical to Claude Code's Task-tool subagent fan-out — the spec must state the concrete mechanism the adlc-prosecute skill will instruct, or document the closest available primitive and any manual-orchestration fallback), and exactly how @adlc/core's dedupeFindings/survivesVerification/shouldContinue get reused (via a new plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecutor.mjs shim, mirroring plugins/adlc-claude-code/lib/prosecutor.mjs's structure).

=== DELIVERABLES ===
1. Five lens agents. Add plugins/adlc-codex/agents/adlc-prosecutor-{correctness,security,contract,diff,tests}.toml, each read-only (sandbox_mode = "read-only"), each with a developer_instructions block adapted from the corresponding plugins/adlc-claude-code/agents/prosecutor-*.md brief (same hunted failure classes, same JSON finding schema: severity/file/line_start/line_end/title/body/evidence/recommendation).
2. Verifier agent. Add plugins/adlc-codex/agents/adlc-prosecutor-verifier.toml adapted from plugins/adlc-claude-code/agents/prosecutor-verifier.md — independent refutation per deduped finding, default-to-refuted on weak evidence, returns { real, reason, repro }.
3. Orchestration shim. Add plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecutor.mjs re-exporting LENSES/VERIFIER/ALL_AGENTS/findingKey/dedupeFindings/survivesVerification/shouldContinue from @adlc/core by reference (no copies), mirroring plugins/adlc-claude-code/lib/prosecutor.mjs. Add an @adlc/core dependency to plugins/adlc-codex/package.json if it is not already resolvable transitively through @adlc/cli.
4. Orchestrating skill update. Rewrite plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc-prosecute/SKILL.md so it no longer says the skill "does not run the reviewer by itself" without qualification — it must document the fan-out to dedupe to independent-verify to loop-until-two-dry-rounds sequence explicitly, name each of the five lens agents plus the verifier by their new file names, and only then describe recording evidence via `adlc prosecute`.
5. Tests. Add plugins/adlc-codex/lib/test/prosecutor-delegation.test.mjs (mirroring plugins/adlc-claude-code/lib/test/prosecutor-delegation.test.mjs) asserting reference-equality between the shim's exports and @adlc/core's.
6. Docs. Update docs/integrations/codex.md and apps/docs/content/docs/integrations/codex.mdx to describe the fan-out — describe reality, not aspiration, if the concrete invocation mechanism turns out to require a documented manual loop rather than automatic execution.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
- AC1: plugins/adlc-codex/agents/adlc-prosecutor-{correctness,security,contract,diff,tests,verifier}.toml exist, each read-only, each with a developer_instructions block naming its lens's specific hunted failure classes. VERIFY: a new plugins/adlc-codex/agents/test/profiles.test.mjs asserting file presence and required TOML keys.
- AC2: plugins/adlc-codex/lib/prosecutor.mjs exports the same bindings as plugins/adlc-claude-code/lib/prosecutor.mjs, verified by reference equality against @adlc/core. VERIFY: node --test plugins/adlc-codex/lib/test/prosecutor-delegation.test.mjs.
- AC3: plugins/adlc-codex/skills/adlc-prosecute/SKILL.md documents the full fan-out/dedupe/verify/loop-until-dry sequence and no longer states the skill "does not run the reviewer by itself" without qualification. VERIFY: a smoke test asserting the SKILL.md body contains the required section markers.
- AC4: `adlc rails-guard --base main --ticket T48` passes when enforcement applies; `npm test` passes at the root.
- AC5: No behavior change to existing @adlc/core prosecutor exports (dedupe/verify/loop logic is reused, not reimplemented). VERIFY: prosecutor-delegation test plus a diff review confirming packages/core/lib/prosecutor.mjs is untouched.

=== OUT OF SCOPE ===
- Changing plugins/adlc-claude-code's prosecutor implementation (source of truth stays there; Codex ports from it, not the reverse).
- Building a generic cross-harness subagent-fan-out primitive — this ticket documents Codex's actual best-available mechanism, however manual, rather than inventing new Codex platform capability.
- T52's MCP/compaction work (separate ticket).
title: Port Claude Code's multi-lens P5 prosecutor fan-out to Codex
